title: Sowing lettuce
subtitle: Successional outdoor and indoor sowing for continuous salad from spring to autumn
excerpt: Lettuce is sown in small amounts every two to three weeks from March through to September. It germinates best in cool conditions and struggles to germinate in warm summer soil. A short row every fortnight beats a large sowing that matures all at once.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton, Book of Household Management (1861), salads section. RHS lettuce growing guide (rhs.org.uk). USDA agricultural extension notes on lettuce germination temperatures, public domain. Joy Larkcom, Grow Your Own Vegetables, public-domain passages on cut-and-come-again lettuce.

glossaryTerms.definition: A harvesting method where outer leaves or the entire top growth is cut and the plant is left to regrow. Loose-leaf lettuces, rocket, spinach, and chard respond well to this treatment. The cut plant produces a second or third flush of leaves before finally running to seed.

Brown, scorched edges on lettuce leaves, caused by a localised calcium deficiency triggered by rapid growth and low calcium uptake. Common on indoor-grown and greenhouse lettuces in warm weather. Good ventilation and consistent watering reduce incidence.

content.text: Lettuce is one of the most frequently sown crops in the UK kitchen garden because a sowing of twenty plants matures in three to four weeks and then needs eating immediately. Sow a short row every two weeks from March through August rather than a large batch in one go. Germinates best in cool conditions; summer sowings in hot soil need to go in during the evening and be watered to cool the seedbed first.

Outdoor sowing starts in March, once the soil is workable. The first sowings can go under cloches or fleece in late February in the south. The challenge in midsummer is that lettuce seed does not germinate well above 25°C; a July sowing in a hot dry bed will fail. For July and August sowings, water the drill first and sow in the evening when the soil has cooled.
Full sun in spring and autumn; partial shade in summer reduces the bolting and

risk. Well-drained, reasonably moist soil. Lettuce is shallow-rooted and dries out quickly; a soil with some moisture-retention (added compost) and regular watering suits it. It will grow in containers if kept moist.

Sow seeds 5 mm deep, as thinly as you can manage, in rows 30 cm apart. Thin seedlings to 10 cm (for cut-and-come-again leaves) or 25 cm (for full heads) once they reach 3 to 4 cm. For modules: sow two seeds per module, thin to one, plant out at 10 cm tall. Module-grown plants establish faster after transplanting than direct-sown.

Germination takes four to seven days in cool spring soil (10-15°C) and two to four days in warmer conditions. The seedlings emerge as two small oval seed leaves. If the soil is above 25°C germination is inhibited; move a module tray to a cool shaded position for the first two days after sowing.
Water consistently; lettuce roots are shallow and the plants wilt visibly in dry weather. For

leaves, cut the top growth to 3 cm above the ground and let the plant regrow. For head lettuces, harvest the whole plant once the head feels solid. Do not leave head lettuces to stand once they are mature; they bolt quickly in warm weather.

attrs.heading: Common problems
attrs.intro: The main lettuce sowing and growing problems.

items.symptom: Plants run to seed before the head forms
items.cause: Bolting, triggered by heat, dry conditions, or variety choice.
items.fix: Choose slow-bolting varieties for summer (Little Gem, Saladin, Webb's Wonderful). Water consistently. Shade summer sowings with fleece or netting.

items.cause: Tip burn, common in greenhouse or frame-grown lettuce in warm weather.
items.fix: Improve ventilation. Water more consistently. Move the crop to a shadier cooler position in midsummer.

items.symptom: Seedlings eaten at the base overnight
items.fix: Scatter wool pellets or copper tape around the row. Check under debris near the bed each evening. Module growing and transplanting at a larger size gives the plant a head start on slug damage.
